title: Disambiguate error types
body:
The gpls `ptrtoerror` linter ( https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/gopls/internal/analysis/ptrtoerror ) flags error types which can be error values, and don't have a call site showing consistent usage, as "it's unclear whether this should be matched as a value type or as a pointer type". Disambiguate the semantics, the way the linter recommends.

Should not change behavior.

comments.body:
That only works in that example because `CustomError` does not define `Error` (in that example, they have an `Unwrap` method, and embed `error` as an anonymous field).

In our case, neither applies: there already is an `Error` method, and the type does not conform to `error` without that method.

The trouble is that this compiles:
```go
var _ error = ManifestTypeRejectedError{} // by value
var _ error = (*ManifestTypeRejectedError)(nil) // by pointer
```
and the linter would like to know which one to expect. It warns if there are both kinds of uses, like in the snippet just above, and it warns if there are zero kinds of uses. (We do use the types, of course, but that’s in other subpackages than the definition.)

but cant we switch `func (e BadPartialRequestError) Error()` to `func (e *BadPartialRequestError) Error()`?
That means error is only implemented for the pointer receiver so only returning `&BadPartialRequestError` would be valid and as such callers should only match `*BadPartialRequestError`?

We can do that for `BadPartialRequestError`, but not for public-API `ManifestTypeRejectedError`. And it would mean an extra allocation — overall, I think that’s not worth it, but I also care very little.

I mean I care also very little, personally I find this go pattern of `var _ error = ManifestTypeRejectedError{}` to check that type X implements an interface type rather ugly and a language failure but that besides the point of this PR naturally.
